papers.title: Preconditioning across Parameter Space for the Parametric Helmholtz Equation
papers.abstract: Abstract. In this work, we address the efficient computation of parameterized systems of linear equations, with possible nonlinear parameter dependence. When the matrix is highly sensitive to the parameters, mean-based preconditioning might not be enough. For this scenario, we explore an approach in which several preconditioners are placed in the parameter space during a precomputation step. To determine the optimal placement of a limited number of preconditioners, we estimate the expected number of iterations with respect to a given preconditioner a priori and use a location-allocation strategy to optimize the placement of the preconditioners. We elaborate on our methodology for the Helmholtz problem with exterior Dirichlet scattering at high frequencies, and we estimate the expected number of GMRES iterations via a gray-box Gaussian process regression approach. We illustrate our approach in two practical applications: scattering in a domain with a parametric refractive index and scattering from a scatterer with parameterized shape. Using these numerical examples, we show how our methods lead to runtime savings of about an order of magnitude. Moreover, we investigate the effect of the parameter dimension and the importance of dimension anisotropy on their efficacy. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/woutervanharten/DistributedPreconditioning and in the supplementary materials ( M174782_Supplementary_Materials_1.pdf [290KB], DistributedPreconditioning-main.zip [753KB]). papers.title: Tangent-plane evidential uncertainty in active learning for magnetic interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: Magnetic interatomic potentials need to account for coupled lattice and spin degrees of freedom, yet constructing reliable training sets remains costly because noncollinear first-principles labels are expensive. Active learning can mitigate this cost, provided that the uncertainty estimate is physically meaningful for the magnetic-response targets that drive spin reorientation. Here we extend the $\mathrm{e}^2\mathrm{IP}$ evidential framework to magnetic machine-learning interatomic potentials by formulating the projected spin-force likelihood and the corresponding epistemic uncertainty in the tangent plane orthogonal to the local spin direction. This construction prevents the uncertainty model from allocating probability mass to a radial spin component that is absent from the constrained-moment supervision. Using bulk BiFeO$_3$ and monolayer CrTe$_2$ as benchmark systems, we show that the resulting tangent-plane epistemic uncertainty indicator $U_{\mathrm{epi}}^{\mathrm{sf}}$ correlates strongly with prediction error and selects more informative configurations than random sampling, simultaneously improving energy, force, and projected spin-force accuracy. These results demonstrate a physically interpretable and data-efficient route for constructing uncertainty-aware magnetic machine-learning interatomic potentials.

papers.title: A Fresh Look at Best Inductive Loop Invariant Synthesis for Bit-Vector Relations
papers.abstract: Synthesizing best inductive invariants (BII) is fundamental to program analysis and verification, yet existing approaches face significant efficiency challenges. We introduce a new formulation for the problem through the lens of mathematical optimization over quantified constraints in first-order theories. The formulation offers a constructive and operational perspective on the BII problem and opens new algorithmic avenues. Building on this formulation, we present two new algorithms for bit-vector programs: a strategically guided linear search that exploits the lattice structure and a bitwise greedy approach that resolves bound bits from high to low with a solver-call count linear in bit-width. We evaluate our approach on a comprehensive benchmark suite, demonstrating significant performance improvements over conventional methods based on symbolic abstraction and chaotic iteration. Experimental results demonstrate our approach solves up to 86% more benchmarks than baseline methods, with improved scaling in solver-call count for high bit-widths and improved verification effectiveness when integrated with k-induction.

papers.title: Physics-constrained inference of somatic dynamics from dendritic recordings with sparse somatic supervision in weakly coupled two-compartment neuron model
papers.abstract: Somatic membrane potential is the primary determinant of neuronal output, yet it remains inaccessible in many experimental setups where only dendritic recordings are available. Reconstructing somatic dynamics from distal measurements is a challenging inverse problem, particularly when the soma and dendrites are weakly coupled, as dendritic signals represent a filtered and attenuated version of somatic activity. To address this, we use a physics-informed neural network (PINN) constrained by a two-compartment Hodgkin--Huxley model. The network is trained on dense dendritic voltage recordings and the known injected current, complemented by a small number of somatic voltage samples (at most 5\% of the time points), and it reconstructs the full somatic trajectory while adjusting a selected set of somatic maximal conductances. On synthetic data from four stimulation protocols, we quantify how the reconstruction depends on the amount of somatic supervision. Without somatic samples, the present formulation returns a smooth trajectory in which the action potentials are absent and the subthreshold level is biased, with a root-mean-square error of 10--14~mV; 1\% of the somatic time points is enough to recover every spike; and 5\% brings the root-mean-square error to about 2~mV, spikes included, with relative errors below 0.1\% on the sodium and delayed-rectifier conductances. We also compare the PINN with an unscented Kalman filter constrained by the same model and assimilating the same observations, and we assess robustness to measurement noise and to random initialization. The reconstructions reported here therefore rely on sparse somatic anchoring in addition to the dendritic recordings. The results delimit what can be inferred in this synthetic, weakly supervised two-compartment setting and identify the amount of somatic information required by the present formulation.

papers.title: A hierarchical adaptive Fourier-feature physics-informed neural network for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma discharges
papers.abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are difficult to train for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF-CCP) fluid--Poisson systems because missing initial conditions, steep sheath gradients, and strongly imbalanced residuals can lead to unstable or nonunique reconstructions. We propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Fourier-feature PINN (HA-FPINN) for such coupled plasma models. The method combines Fourier feature mapping to improve the representation of small-scale sheath structures, sparse physical anchors to provide interior constraints, and a two-level adaptive weighting scheme to balance the PDE, boundary, and anchor losses as well as individual equation residuals. The framework is tested on an 8-equation helium discharge model and a 23-equation electronegative \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) model. In the helium case, HA-FPINN reconstructs the space--time evolution of the main physical variables with \(1\%\) anchors and converges for all tested network architectures, with convergence times of \(110\)--\(246\) s. In the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case, HA-FPINN achieves stable reconstruction with \(5\%\) anchors, whereas the non-adaptive Fourier-feature PINN and standard PINN fail to converge under the same setting. The best performance in both systems is obtained at the tested Fourier frequency parameter \(\sigma=2.20\). Noise-injection tests show that HA-FPINN maintains the lowest reconstruction error in the helium case and preserves the main space--time structures in the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case up to \(15\%\) anchor noise. These results show that HA-FPINN provides a robust PINN formulation for strongly coupled plasma fluid models with missing initial conditions.

papers.title: Optical imaging framework for melt pool monitoring and bead geometry prediction in blown powder directed energy deposition
papers.abstract: Abstract Blown powder laser directed energy deposition (DED-LP) is an emerging additive manufacturing process with applications in both new part manufacture and repair of high-value components. However, the deposition of consistent bead geometry requires precise control of melt pool dynamics. While in-situ monitoring methods have been developed, linking melt pool optical signals to solidified geometry remains an open challenge. Monocular imaging offers a low-cost, minimally invasive sensing approach, yet is inherently indirect due to projection effects and process-induced optical variability. This work presents a monitoring framework to interpret melt pool images by analytical and data-driven means. Contours detected from intensity-based image segmentation are translated to world coordinates using affine projection to provide calibration-based geometric proxies for comparison with solidified bead geometry. At nominal printing conditions, the analytical approach yielded mean absolute percentage errors of 2.5 % for bead width and 16.2 % for bead height. The affine projection method captured trends in solidified bead geometry across the traverse speed and laser power ranges investigated within the material-specific operating envelope. To refine estimates, a Gaussian process regression model (GPR) was trained on image-derived features and process conditions. GPR achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 1.4 % for width and 3.7 % for height across the tested traverse speed conditions. This study demonstrates the applicability of analytical interpretations of monocular melt pool images for analysis within the standard operating window of 316L stainless steel feedstock and demonstrates how GPR may be leveraged to learn underlying relationships not captured by analytical intensity-based image segmentation.

papers.title: Effect of printing layer thickness and sintering time on the densification, microstructure and mechanical properties of binder-jetted Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: This study examines how printing layer thickness and sintering time jointly affect the densification, microstructure, and tensile behavior of binder-jetted Ti-6Al-4V under a fixed jetting strategy. Specimens were printed with layer thicknesses of 40, 80, and 120 μm and sintered at 1300 °C for 1–5 h. Reducing the layer thickness increased green density and refined the initial pore structure, thereby accelerating pore closure during early sintering. The 40 μm specimens reached the best condition after 2 h, with 94.4% relative density, 4.4% porosity, and an ultimate tensile strength approaches the wrought benchmark. Larger layer thicknesses required longer holding times but showed lower maximum densities within the investigated process window. Prolonged holding also promoted grain growth and possible pore coarsening, which limited further improvement. These results indicate that improving the green-body state by reducing layer thickness is more effective than simply extending sintering time, although ductility and residual defect control remain important for further optimization.

papers.title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

papers.title: The Moderating Role of Social Support in the Relationship Between Diabetes Distress and Psychological Well‐Being Among Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross‐Sectional Study Protocol
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Type 2 diabetes imposes a considerable psychological burden on older adults, including elevated diabetes distress and diminished psychological well‐being. Social support may buffer the harmful mental‐health effects of chronic disease‐related stress, yet whether it moderates the link between diabetes distress and psychological well‐being remains rarely examined among older Iranian adults with type 2 diabetes. This protocol aims to determine the moderating role of social support in that relationship in this population. Methods This descriptive‐analytic cross‐sectional protocol will recruit 300 adults aged 60 years or above with type 2 diabetes from the Bandar Abbas Diabetes Clinic through simple random sampling from the clinic electronic registry. Trained interviewers will administer a demographic and clinical form, the age‐adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, the PAID‐5 (diabetes distress), the MSSS‐5 (social support), and the WHO‐5 Well‐Being Index in person or by telephone using identical structured interviews. Hierarchical multiple regression will test the diabetes distress by social support interaction on WHO‐5 scores, in an unadjusted model and a model adjusted for a pre‐specified demographic and clinical covariate set, with heteroscedasticity‐robust standard errors, bootstrapped confidence intervals, and simple‐slopes and Johnson‐Neyman probing. Missing data will be handled with multiple imputation. Analyses will use IBM SPSS Statistics version 28 with two‐sided tests at α = 0.05. Results As a protocol, no empirical results are reported. The completed study will yield estimates of diabetes distress, social support, and psychological well‐being levels, their bivariate associations, and the moderation effect with appropriate uncertainty quantification. Conclusion The findings are expected to provide a scientific basis for nursing and psychosocial interventions that strengthen social support networks to protect the psychological well‐being of older adults with type 2 diabetes. Ethical approval has been obtained (IR.HUMS.REC.1405.013); written or audio‐recorded verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

papers.title: Diffusion-RarePHM: A Physics-Constrained Conditional Latent World Model for Multi-Future Degradation Forecasting and Rare-Fault Prognostics
papers.abstract: Industrial prognostics is constrained less by the abundance of healthy telemetry than by the scarcity, heterogeneity, and operational ambiguity of genuine failure evolution. This study introduces Diffusion-RarePHM, a physics-constrained conditional latent world model that converts heterogeneous monitoring streams into probabilistic, multi-future degradation scenarios. A unified health encoder maps engine and compressor observations into a common mechanism-oriented health interface with asset-specific fitting, while state-dependent dual-domain dynamics couple latent health levels with their increments. Conditioned on current health, equipment structure, prospective duty, environment, maintenance action, and target fault mode, latent diffusion generates an ensemble of complete future trajectories. Rare precursors are synthesized as physically directed departures from normal latent evolution and screened by physical, dynamic, and explicit temporal-predicate semantic criteria. The study draws from PHM2024 and MetroPT3 source archives containing 742,625 and 1,516,948 records, respectively; deterministic PHM2024 subsets and 12,642 chronologically retained MetroPT3 observations are used for the reported experiments. On the PHM2024 record-level held-out diagnosis partition, the model attained 98.23% accuracy, 98.16% macro-F1, and 0.9985 AUROC. Across held-out operating-condition groups, it attained 97.86±0.12% accuracy, 97.77±0.13% macro-F1, and 0.9979±0.0003 AUROC over five training seeds. In the MetroPT3-anchored controlled semi-physical benchmark, reconstruction of prescribed health trajectories achieved nine-scenario averages of 2.250 percentage-point RMSE, 2.294% MAPE, and 90.00% pointwise constructed-reference coverage for the nominal 90% interval. Controlled trajectory experiments examine the generator’s response to prescribed precursors, leakage, compound degradation, maintenance, thermal-load stress, and observation corruption, together with their first-passage and tail-risk functionals. The trajectory evidence establishes mechanism-conditioned generation and reconstruction of controlled degradation scenarios, with accepted-path warning, first-passage, and tail-risk statistics derived under the specified dynamics and interventions.

papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) of high-γ′ Ni-based superalloys is limited by cracking and microstructural heterogeneity. Here, a flat top (FT) laser beam was used to fabricate Inconel 939, and its cracking behaviour, microstructure, and tensile properties were compared with those produced by a Gaussian beam. At 850 W and 350 mm/s, FT-LPBF produced specimens with 99.95% relative density and no cracks detected in the examined sections. Compared with the Gaussian conditions, FT processing generated flatter melt pools, continuous columnar grains, and a lower fraction of high-angle grain boundaries. The as-built FT specimen achieved an ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 1211 MPa and elongation of 18.8% at room temperature. From 800–1000°C, its UTS decreased from 983 to 284 MPa, while elongation increased from 18.4% to 29.4%. Thermal-fluid simulations suggest that a more uniform temperature field and reduced lateral thermal gradients contribute to stable epitaxial growth. These findings demonstrate that a more uniformly distributed laser beam profile can improve the printability and tensile performance of IN939 without post-processing.

papers.title: Dynamic Prediction of Drought and Flood Catastrophes Under Climate Change: A Coupled GM(1,1)–Weibull–Bootstrap Model for Zhengzhou, China (1951–2024)
papers.abstract: Drought and flood catastrophes threaten water security in the Yellow River Basin, yet prediction is hampered by sparse extreme event records. This study couples catastrophe series extraction via GM(1,1), Weibull extreme value modeling, and bootstrap uncertainty quantification, applying it to 74 years (1951–2024) of annual precipitation in Zhengzhou, China. Percentile thresholds of 410 mm (drought) and 864.6 mm (extreme precipitation) yield five drought and seven extreme precipitation catastrophe years. Both Weibull fits pass three goodness-of-fit tests, whereas the GM(1,1) benchmark fails for the flood series (mean error 21.5% vs. 3.31% for drought). The 0.9 quantile recurrence times (17.8 and 22.9 years) project the next drought catastrophe around 2031 (90% bootstrap window 2025–2033) and the next extreme precipitation catastrophe around 2044 (2034–2047); conditional residual life forecasts shift these by only 1–2 years (to 2033 and 2045, respectively). Two truncated record hindcasts (2013 drought; 2003 flood) fell within the predicted windows, and threshold perturbation and alternative distribution analyses support their robustness. Divergent shape parameters (k = 2.47 vs. 1.29) reveal accelerating drought but decelerating extreme precipitation hazard, providing probabilistic lead times for disaster risk management in data-scarce regions.

papers.title: Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states
papers.abstract: Human performance often fails not because latent capacity is absent, but because access to high-functioning cognitive states is unstable under fatigue, distraction, overload, and pressure. This hypothesis paper proposes closed-loop cognitive state control—informally, supercognition —as a neuroengineering objective: rapid entry into, stabilization of, and recovery of an individual's highest available task-specific cognitive state. The framework treats cognition as a partially observable dynamical system whose latent states would be inferred from multimodal behavioral, physiological, contextual, and neural signals, and specifies a five-layer architecture comprising multimodal sensing, latent-state inference, predictive transition modeling, closed-loop intervention, and a longitudinal personal neural twin. The proposal is situated against existing closed-loop and neuroadaptive architectures, with an explicit statement of what is and is not new. The state ontology is given as a set of falsifiable assumptions rather than an intuitive taxonomy. Candidate computational implementations are specified for each layer, including hidden semi-Markov and switching state-space models, Bayesian and Kalman filtering, sequence models, hazard models, contextual bandits, model-predictive control, and offline reinforcement learning. The personal neural twin receives an operational specification covering its data requirements, update schedule, calibration and drift-monitoring criteria, and failure modes. Predictive and causal claims are separated, with the evidentiary requirements stated for each. The paper engages directly with the literature that challenges the framework's feasibility, including biomarker reliability, mixed neurofeedback findings, cross-task and cross-subject generalization failure, and the ecological-validity gap in wearable neurotechnology. Operational definitions, application scenarios, a validation protocol with power and diversity requirements, an expanded ethics and governance analysis, and a staged research roadmap are provided. No component of the architecture has been implemented or evaluated here: no simulation, clinical trial, or empirical efficacy claim is presented, and the validation programme described is prospective. The contribution is a falsifiable systems-engineering hypothesis for cognitive-state control.

papers.title: Weldability of Additively Manufactured Austenitic Stainless Steels
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) can enable faster, lower-cost production of power generation components. However, implementation of AM parts into service requires welding to other components, and the weldability of AM alloys is not well characterized. On-cooling hot ductility testing was performed between 1000°C and 1300°C on gas metal arc directed energy deposition (GMADED), laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), and wrought 316-series stainless steels to evaluate weldability and ductility dip cracking (DDC) susceptibility of AM austenitic stainless steels. The results were analyzed with respect to variations in dynamic recrystallization, absorbed energy, and fracture mechanism. Single and multipass autogenous gas tungsten arc welds were performed on GMADED, L-PBF, and wrought plates to correlate hot ductility behavior with DDC susceptibility in welded specimens. GMA-DED 316(L/H/LSi) exhibited good hot ductility regardless of post-build heat treatment, while L-PBF 316L exhibited reduced ductility across all conditions. L-PBF 316L also exhibited lower absorbed energy, which correlated with reduced hot ductility and intergranular fracture, whereas the GMA-DED and wrought conditions exhibited greater absorbed energy and ductile fracture. The reduced weldability of L-PBF 316L is suggested to be associated with grain boundary embrittlement from impurity elements segregation during primary austenite solidification. Heat-affected zone microcracking was observed in the GTAW welds of L-PBF 316L, confirming susceptibility to DDC and supporting the correlation between reduced hot ductility and weldability issues.

papers.title: Flat-top laser powder bed fusion of non-weldable Ni-based superalloy: crack mitigation through microstructural engineering for enhanced mechanical properties
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) of high-γ′ Ni-based superalloys is limited by cracking and microstructural heterogeneity. Here, a flat top (FT) laser beam was used to fabricate Inconel 939, and its cracking behaviour, microstructure, and tensile properties were compared with those produced by a Gaussian beam. At 850 W and 350 mm/s, FT-LPBF produced specimens with 99.95% relative density and no cracks detected in the examined sections. Compared with the Gaussian conditions, FT processing generated flatter melt pools, continuous columnar grains, and a lower fraction of high-angle grain boundaries. The as-built FT specimen achieved an ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 1211 MPa and elongation of 18.8% at room temperature. From 800–1000°C, its UTS decreased from 983 to 284 MPa, while elongation increased from 18.4% to 29.4%. Thermal-fluid simulations suggest that a more uniform temperature field and reduced lateral thermal gradients contribute to stable epitaxial growth. These findings demonstrate that a more uniformly distributed laser beam profile can improve the printability and tensile performance of IN939 without post-processing.

papers.title: Prioritizing career readiness by humanizing STEM for undergraduate education success
papers.abstract: Abstract STEM-focused and social science skill sets will be required to successfully address many current global problems. Although providing active learning, communication, and technological skills—often lacking in current curricular approaches—is essential for STEM student success, they alone are insufficient to recruit, prepare, and retain students for rapidly evolving STEM careers. Here, we review practices that, by humanizing STEM, act to both entice students and prioritize their STEM career readiness. We promote combining the development of science career skills with social competencies through student-centered teaching aligned with university-wide, interdepartmental collaboration and community engagement. We explore how the ESA-endorsed, multidimensional ecology education curricular framework (4DEE) can promote career readiness in ecology and other biological and STEM disciplines. Finally, we discuss how to implement teaching and mentoring changes that can increase student and faculty success, strengthen departmental/institutional support for STEM career development, and enhance societal well-being and sustainability.

papers.title: Predicting knee pain severity in professional distance runners using gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Background Knee pain is common in runners and may precede injury; clinical labels are sparse, but repeated symptom monitoring is practical for training decisions. The purpose of this paper is to develop a probabilistic, interpretable model that predicts a continuous knee pain severity score in professional distance runners using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and to quantify the relative influence of routinely measurable training and anthropometric variables. Methods Fifty professional male distance runners aged 20–30 years were recruited from professional athletics in Ankara, Turkey. Six predictors were used: resistance training frequency, weekly running distance, training surface, running technique (foot-strike category), history of prior knee problems, and body mass index (BMI). The outcome was a continuous knee pain severity score normalized to 0–1 from a self-reported numerical rating scale. A GPR model with a radial basis function kernel was trained using a train-test split and evaluated with mean squared error (MSE). Results Prediction uncertainty was quantified using 95% credible intervals, and sensitivity analysis were performed to assess feature influence. The GPR model achieved low prediction error on the held-out test set [MSE = (0.02)] and stable performance under cross-validation [mean MSE = (0.028)]. Conclusion Sensitivity analysis showed pronounced GPR response patterns for resistance training frequency and BMI, with smaller response patterns for weekly running distance and prior knee problems/injuries. Training surface and running technique showed comparatively limited sensitivity. GPR effectively models self-reported pain with uncertainty quantification and is scalable for symptom-based risk assessment, though not intended for clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Wound Dressings for the Treatment of Diabetic Wounds: A Brief Review of Modern Approaches and Clinical Perspectives
papers.abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major global health concern, with its prevalence projected to increase significantly in the coming decades. One of the most severe complications of DM is the development of chronic wounds, particularly diabetic foot ulcers, which contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Effective wound management is essential to mitigate these impacts, and wound dressings play a central role in promoting proper healing. This review provides a brief overview of the general status of wound dressings used for diabetic wound care, highlighting the evolution from traditional dressings to modern, bioactive alternatives. Key polymeric materials and strategies incorporated into current dressings are discussed, including hydrocolloids, hydrogels, alginates, and nanomaterials. The review also addresses critical challenges, such as the high cost and limited accessibility of advanced dressings in low- and middle-income countries, as well as emerging innovations like smart dressings with embedded sensors and 3D bioprinting technologies. Future efforts must focus on improving the efficacy, affordability, and availability of advanced wound care solutions to meet the growing global burden of diabetic wounds.

papers.title: Hierarchical MCTS-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Co-designing Formulation and Processing of Thermosetting Polymers with Balanced Performance
papers.abstract: Abstract Optimizing the properties of thermosetting polymers presents an inherent challenge due to the high-dimensional formulation-processing parameter space and the trade-offs between thermomechanical properties. In this contribution, we propose a hierarchical Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS)-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to enable the simultaneous design of both the composition and curing protocols of epoxy resins as a major class of thermosetting polymers. A sigmoid-based weighting strategy is introduced to encode application-driven performance thresholds into the objective function, guiding the optimization toward coordinated multi-property improvement. With only 30 experiments across four iterative rounds, the framework optimizes both the formulation and curing protocols to yield a performance-enhanced epoxy resin that simultaneously meets all four target thresholds. This balanced performance cannot be achieved by any of the initial samples, an equal-weight baseline, or commercial and literature-reported systems. Furthermore, interpretable machine learning analysis combined with targeted experimental validation quantitatively resolves the relative importance of formulation and processing parameters, indicating that composition variables dominate overall property trends while their synergistic interactions produce non-linear effects on glass transition temperature. The findings demonstrate that the hierarchical MCTS-guided BO framework offers an efficient strategy for navigating complex formulation-processing spaces, and the interpretable analysis provides a quantitative basis for understanding structure–property relationships in thermosetting polymers.

papers.title: Nonlinear model predictive control method for autonomous approach of tanker/receiver
papers.abstract: Abstract In order to solve the problems of strong nonlinearity, strong coupling and multivariable constraints of the receiverr’s motion model in the process of the tanker/receiver autonomous approach, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) method is proposed in this paper. By analysing the external forces and torques acting on the receiver, a nonlinear dynamic model of the receiver is established to provide an accurate prediction model for NMPC. An objective function with the terminal state of the receiver is designed, multiple state variable constraints are added, the adaptive gradient descent method is used to solve the optimal control quantity online and finally the stability of NMPC is proved. The numerical simulation results show that the proposed method has good control performance and can quickly and stably control the receiver to fly directly behind the tanker and maintain the same speed and direction.

papers.title: MOPSO-Tuned Robust Model Predictive Control of Bidirectional Inductive Power Transfer Systems Under Coupling and Load Uncertainty: Coordinated Voltage and Frequency Support for Grid-Connected Electric Vehicle Charging
papers.abstract: The rapid development of electric vehicles (EVs) creates a need for charging systems that provide convenience and energy efficiency while supporting the electric grid. One possible solution is Bidirectional Inductive Power Transfer (BIPT), which enables contact-less energy transfer between the EV battery and the electric grid. However, variations in magnetic coupling, such as coil misalignments, changes in battery load, and disturbances on the electric grid, can significantly degrade power-transfer efficiency, voltage regulation, and system stability. To address these issues, this research proposes a Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimisation (MOPSO) tuned Robust Model Predictive Control (RMPC) system for grid-connected BIPT systems. This system will combine uncertainty-aware power regulation with coordinated voltage and frequency support. A MATLAB/Simulink model includes bidirectional power converters, series-series resonant compensation, magnetic coupling variations, battery characteristics, and grid-side active and reactive power control. The proposed RMPC strategy accounts for bounded uncertainty in the coupling and load. It optimises voltage tracking, frequency regulation, power-transfer accuracy, and control effort subject to converter and battery constraints. MOPSO will determine Paretooptimal controller parameters, eliminating the traditional trialand-error tuning process. The proposed system will have a nominal power rating of 3.3 kW, an operating frequency of 85 kHz, and a magnetic coupling coefficient ranging from 0.15 to 0.35. Simulation scenarios will include battery resistance variations of plus 20 parcent, grid voltage disturbances of plus 10 parcent, frequency deviations of plus 0.5 Hz, and switching between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid modes of operation. Performance evaluation will compare the proposed system with conventional proportionalintegral control and nominal MPC using voltage tracking error, transient overshoot, settling time, frequency recovery, power transfer efficiency, and compliance with operational constraints. This investigation aims to determine whether the optimised RMPC framework improves disturbance rejection, maintains stable bidirectional energy transfer, and coordinates active and reactive power responses under simultaneous uncertainties. This researchs primary contribution is integrating robust predictive regulation, Multi-objective controller optimisation and coordinated grid support capabilities into a single wireless charging architecture. This proposed approach may increase charging reliability, reduce sensitivity to coil misalignment, and enable EV batteries to play a greater role in enhancing grid flexibility and integrating renewable energy sources. However, this approach needs experimental verification and an assessment of real-time computational requirements, battery degradation, communication reliability, and hardware limitations. This study provides a systematic approach for evaluating intelligent, grid-responsive wireless EV charging, which could lead to more robust electric grids, more sustainable transportation infrastructure, and the transition toward low-carbon mobility.

papers.title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
papers.abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington’s disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis. Here, the authors introduce scBOA, a Bayesian optimization tool that helps researchers choose single-cell analysis settings for cell-type annotation. They perform benchmarking to show that performance depends on the dataset, reference and objective.

papers.title: Concentration-Driven Tuning of Structural, Electronic, Magnetic, and Optical Properties in Fe-Doped Anatase TiO2: A Hybrid FP-LAPW GGA/GGA+U and PINN Investigation
papers.abstract: A concentration-dependent investigation of Fe-doped anatase TiO2 was performed using the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method implemented in WIEN2k, combined with GGA, GGA+U, and physics-informed neural network (PINN) modeling. Fe concentrations of 3.125%, 6.25%, 12.5%, and 25% were examined using 2 × 2 × 2 anatase TiO2 supercells. Fe incorporation systematically expands the anatase lattice, with the equilibrium volume increasing from 17.14 Å3/f.u. for pristine TiO2 to 18.49 Å3/f.u. within GGA and up to 18.91 Å3/f.u. using Hubbard-corrected treatments at 25% Fe. The bulk modulus decreases from 179.2 GPa to 160.5 GPa in GGA, indicating concentration-driven lattice softening, while the formation energy becomes more negative, reaching −10.91 eV/f.u. for GGA+UTi+UFe at 25% Fe. Electronically, Fe doping introduces localized Fe-3d impurity states within the forbidden gap, narrowing the band gap from 2.18 eV for pristine TiO2 to 1.23 eV in GGA and to 1.59 eV in GGA+UTi+UFe at 25% Fe. The ferromagnetic magnetic moment increases with Fe concentration, reaching 4.41 μB/f.u. for the combined Hubbard correction. Optical calculations reveal enhanced dielectric, conductivity, absorption, reflectivity, and loss responses in the visible-to-near-UV range due to Fe-3d/O-2p/Ti-3d hybridization. The PINN model closely reproduces the FP-LAPW/GGA+U trends, including band gaps from 2.25 eV at 3.125% Fe to 1.48 eV at 25% Fe, demonstrating its usefulness as an efficient surrogate for correlated-property prediction. These results establish Fe doping as an effective route for multifunctional tuning of anatase TiO2 for photocatalytic, photovoltaic, optoelectronic, and spintronic applications.

papers.title: Neutrosophic Weighting of Epidemiological Criteria Using Jensen–Shannon Divergence: An Extended CRITIC Method for Prioritizing Parasitic Species in Public Health
papers.abstract: Intestinal parasitic infections remain a significant public health burden in resource-limited settings, yet prioritization of species for surveillance and intervention is complicated by incomplete epidemiological data and conflicting criteria. This study addresses the problem of ranking eight intestinal parasite species under uncertainty using data from 110 patients across five clinical and epidemiological criteria: prevalence, abnormal consistency, mucus rate, coinfection, and diarrhea rate. We propose a novel framework that integrates (i) Wilson confidence intervals and bootstrapping to quantify estimation uncertainty; (ii) single-valued neutrosophic sets to capture truth, indeterminacy, and falsity; (iii) an extended CRITIC method employing Jensen–Shannon divergence instead of Pearson correlation to capture non-linear relationships between criteria; and (iv) the MARCOS method for final ranking. The results show that under the proposed neutrosophication, mucus rate emerges as the most influential criterion (weight = 0.3038) under Jensen–Shannon divergence, while abnormal consistency rate becomes the second most important (0.2135), and coinfection receives a moderate but non-negligible weight (0.1659). The ranking is stable at the extreme positions across the four dissimilarity functions tested, with Ascaris lumbricoides and Entamoeba coli consistently occupying the top two positions (though the order varies by method), and Giardia lamblia is consistently last. The main theoretical contribution is the integration of uncertainty quantification, neutrosophication, and non-linear divergence into a single MCDM framework. From a practical perspective, the results provide actionable priorities for screening programs, with mucus rate recommended as a key clinical indicator for surveillance.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Digital Twin-Enabled Edge Intelligence for Battery Degradation, Thermal Stress, and Energy Management in Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: Abstract Energy-management strategies are needed to coordinate efficient operation, thermal-stress limitation, and battery-health considerations in electric-vehicle (EV) battery systems under varying operating conditions. This paper develops a risk-aware EV battery energy-management framework based on a Digital Twin, combining battery-state prediction, a heuristic uncertainty indicator, thermal-risk assessment, and battery-health information within a unified current-control scheme. The Digital Twin supplies battery-state information to the controller, while the edge-intelligence layer supports local processing without continuous cloud interaction. Five controllers—Rule-Based, Model Predictive Control (MPC), AI-only, Digital Twin-based, and the proposed risk-aware Digital Twin-enabled controller—are evaluated under common simulated conditions. In the nominal simulation, the proposed controller consumes 24.494 kWh, compared with 22.534 kWh for the Rule-Based controller and approximately 25.35–25.54 kWh for the MPC, AI-only, and Digital Twin-based controllers. Its simulated peak temperature is approximately 22.5 °C, compared with approximately 22.7–22.8 °C for the other controllers; however, the small difference is model-dependent and is not interpreted as statistically established thermal superiority. The proposed controller does not achieve the best SOC prediction RMSE, and its higher SOC RMSE illustrates a trade-off between prediction accuracy and risk-aware control. The reported host-side MATLAB latency is approximately 0.00233 ms and is treated only as a preliminary computational indicator, not as an embedded automotive execution benchmark. The results therefore support the feasibility of studying Digital Twin prediction and uncertainty-aware decision-making in a simulation-based EV battery energy-management framework, while the limitations of the reduced aging model, nominal thermal range, statistical evidence, and simulation-only validation are explicitly acknowledged.

papers.title: Drive Structures and Whole-Body Coordinated Control Methods for Humanoid Robots
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots require both high-performance drive structures and effective whole-body coordinated control to achieve dynamic motion, load transportation, and complex whole-body movements. This paper reviews the relationship between mechanical drive design and coordinated control methods for humanoid robots, with particular emphasis on the constraints imposed by actuator torque, mass distribution, transmission characteristics, and real-robot dynamics. At the hardware level, high-torque-density modular joints, lightweight transmissions, hybrid serial-parallel mechanisms, and drive-layout optimisation are examined in terms of their effects on joint torque, moving mass, and motion capability. At the control level, multi-joint coordinated motion control, model predictive control, reinforcement learning, and dynamics adaptation methods are discussed for maintaining stability and improving actuator utilisation under contact and joint constraints. The review further considers the differences between idealised simulation models and physical robots caused by friction, hysteresis, drive-torque deviations, contact compliance, and communication delays. The analysis indicates that drive structures establish the hardware boundaries of humanoid motion capability, while whole-body coordinated control determines how effectively these capabilities can be realised during operation. The paper therefore highlights the importance of integrated electromechanical and control co-design, including joint parameters, drive layouts, mass distribution, state estimation, and dynamics adaptation, as a potential direction for improving the robustness and efficiency of humanoid robots.

papers.title: Actively seeking variability: effects of active learning and talker variability on novel word learning in adults
papers.abstract: Talker variability has been found to be both helpful and challenging for learners. For example, while adult word recognition is slowed down when the talker changes rapidly from trial to trial, this same talker variability can benefit learning non-native sound contrasts and production of novel words. However, all prior research has exposed participants to predetermined orders or variability conditions. Since research suggests that learners engage in active information seeking and it can benefit learning, here we ask whether adults seek out talker variability during word learning and how this variability influences performance. Active participants chose to hear words from 5 talkers on average, and hearing more talker variability for individual words predicted production and comprehension accuracy. While active learning was not beneficial, participants in the Passive condition performed better on the comprehension test. Results are consistent when cognates are excluded from the analyses. We discuss the results in the context of high variability phonetic training and active learning theories.

papers.title: Electrochemical finishing of complex curved internal channels fabricated by metal additive manufacturing using a segmented multi-link cathode
papers.abstract: Abstract The polishing of curved internal channels in metal additive manufacturing remains exceedingly challenging, primarily constrained by the limitations of cathode structures and the intricate geometry of internal channels. To address this issue, an electrochemical finishing method with a segmented multi-link cathode is proposed for the polishing of curved holes fabricated via selective laser melting. Simulation results of stress and offset amount show that the segmented multi-link cathode in the curved hole enables flexible bend to adapt to the channel’s contour. Moreover, the integration of the nylon brush facilitates the alignment of the center of the segmented multi-link cathode with that of the curved hole. Compared with the maximum offset amount of 0.21 mm at the center of the monolithic twisted cathode, the center of the segmented multi-link cathode exhibits negligible deviation. Current density distribution simulations further confirm that a uniform side gap ensures a homogeneous current density distribution during the electrochemical finishing. This uniformity mitigates the occurrence of non-uniform material removal problems, such as overcut polishing and undercut polishing. Consequently, a curved hole with a diameter of 2 mm, a length of 60 mm and a curvature radius of 120 mm is successfully polished. The average surface roughness Ra is reduced from 11.36 μm to 1.59 μm, while the average roundness is improved from 0.138 mm (achieved via conventional electropolishing with monolithic twisted cathode) to 0.011 mm using the proposed method. Furthermore, the proposed method enables the finishing of spiral internal channel with variable curvature radius and reciprocal internal channel with small curvature radius. The average surface roughness Ra of the spiral and reciprocal internal channel are remarkably reduced from 11.80 μm and 11.36 μm to 2.57 μm and 2.80 μm respectively. Such a result cannot be attained using conventional electropolishing, thereby validating the superiority of the proposed method.

papers.title: Digital Dentistry: The Use of 3D Printing in Prosthetic Dentistry
papers.abstract: Background: Three-dimensional (3D) printing has progressed from producing study models and surgical guides to fabricating definitive prostheses. The supporting evidence is scattered across laboratory studies, a small number of clinical trials and several overlapping reviews, so students and early-career clinicians find it hard to judge which applications are actually supported. Methods: This narrative, non-systematic review covers English-language studies published between 2015 and 2026 on printing technologies, materials, accuracy, fit and clinical outcomes of printed prostheses. Studies were identified in PubMed/MEDLINE, their bibliographic details were checked in Crossref, and the findings were synthesised thematically. Results: Resin prosthodontics relies mainly on vat photopolymerisation (SLA, DLP, LCD), whereas selective laser melting is used for cobalt-chromium frameworks. Printed denture bases reached clinically acceptable fit, but milled bases were usually more accurate and stronger in laboratory comparisons, and build orientation, often 45 degrees, affected accuracy. Patient-reported outcomes of printed complete dentures were generally similar to those of conventional dentures, although retention was lower in one meta-analysis. Printed resin crowns performed acceptably in the short term, but one randomised trial found more wear and a numerically higher fracture rate than with zirconia at one year. Evidence on printed zirconia comes mainly from laboratory work, and evidence on maxillofacial prostheses from reported cases and technique descriptions. Conclusions: 3D printing is a workable option for provisional restorations, surgical guides, removable prosthesis bases and frameworks, and selected definitive restorations. Long-term clinical data remain limited, and standardised post-processing and longer trials are needed before routine use for definitive posterior restorations.

papers.title: Using Chatgpt “Teacher Mode” To Teach: A Design-Based Research Protocol and Implementation Framework
papers.abstract: The unstructured use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education may encourage passive answer-seeking rather than active learning. This study introduces ChatGPT Teacher Mode, a structured framework designed to position generative AI as a guided instructional partner that promotes critical thinking, metacognition, and evidence-based reasoning. Using a design-based research approach, the study develops a protocol for implementing Teacher Mode across mathematics, history, civics, and geography. The framework incorporates discipline-specific learning activities, including articulating mathematical reasoning, evaluating primary sources, explaining constitutional principles, and interpreting climate maps. It integrates pedagogical scaffolding, formative assessment, verification routines, and transparent AI-use policies to support responsible implementation. The proposed framework targets four outcomes: improved learning through structured reasoning, enhanced metacognitive awareness, higher-quality feedback aligned with assessment rubrics, and greater transparency in AI use. Potential challenges, including inaccurate outputs, over-reliance, and inequitable access, are addressed through verification strategies, AI-assisted and AI-free assessments, and institutional guidelines. This study contributes a socio-technical framework, an empirically testable research protocol, and practical guidance for educators integrating generative AI into teaching and learning. Teacher Mode offers a structured approach to leveraging generative AI while maintaining academic integrity and supporting meaningful student engagement. Its effectiveness, however, requires empirical validation across educational contexts

papers.title: Automated and noninvasive in vivo mapping of brain functions in the human cortex
papers.abstract: Mapping forms the basis for understanding the functional organization of the brain and for developing targeted interventions in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive tool that allows causal mapping of cortical functions involved in motor control, speech, and connectivity. Since manual mapping procedures limit standardization, we present an automated cortical mapping method that integrates electronically controlled multi-locus TMS with a Bayesian optimization algorithm for identifying stimulation targets efficiently and objectively through a closed-loop framework. We localized individual motor representation area peaks with high accuracy (average 2.4 mm and 5° deviation from the optimum) in only approximately 4 minutes. This represents a substantial advancement over current mapping approaches, providing the means to greatly accelerate and standardize both research and clinical protocols while maintaining high reliability. We anticipate that our approach can further extend to map other cortical functions that cannot be easily analyzed online by a human operator.

papers.title: Kesulitan Belajar Pemrograman dan Strategi Pembelajaran untuk Meningkatkan Pemahaman Mahasiswa: Tinjauan Literatur
papers.abstract: Programming is a key competency in computer science education, but the process of learning it often poses a challenge for students, particularly in courses on basic programming, algorithms, and object-oriented programming. This article aims to summarize the types of difficulties students face when learning programming in higher education as well as the learning strategies reported in previous research. The study was conducted through a directed narrative literature review of journal articles discussing programming difficulties, active learning, blended learning, debugging, formative assessment, learning analytics, pair programming, and artificial intelligence support. Sources were selected based on their relevance to the higher education context, the availability of metadata and abstracts on publishers’ websites, and their relevance to the study’s focus. The synthesis indicates that students’ difficulties are not only related to programming language syntax but also to conceptual understanding, the formation of mental models regarding program execution, problem-solving, coding, and the management of self-directed learning processes. Strategies that may be helpful include gradual and repetitive practice, rapid feedback, formative assessment, active problem-based learning, collaboration, and monitoring of learning progress. AI-based tools can provide assistance and feedback, but they must be used critically because AI outputs are not always correct and can undermine independent thinking if used without guidance this study concludes that programming instruction should combine conceptual explanations, structured practice, reflection on errors, and learning support tailored to students’ needs.

papers.title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF NEURAL NETWORK METHODS FOR SOLVING THE MODEL OF A SINGLE DISLOCATION SOURCE OF GEOACOUSTIC EMISSION
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of computational methods for modeling a single dislocation source of geoacoustic emission radiation, the Berlage oscillator. The paper considers the Rosenbrock numerical method of the fourth order of accuracy, a parallel modification of a physically informed neural network into three subdomains (TriDomainPINN), as well as a neural network based on Legendre polynomials (LeNN). The parallel version of PINN makes it possible to increase the efficiency of the solution and reduce the learning time by decomposing the modeling area. All algorithms are implemented in Python using the PyTorch library; the implementation provides a mechanism for early stopping of network training and the distribution of collocation points according to Chebyshev’s law. Accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency were evaluated for each method. Numerical experiments show that the Legendre polynomial network provides high approximation accuracy with a significant reduction in computational costs and time.

papers.title: Causality-enhanced and symmetry-preserving PINNs for damped elastodynamic PDEs
papers.abstract: This study develops a causality-enhanced and symmetry-preserving Physics-Informed Neural Network (S-PINN) framework for nonlinear damped elastodynamic partial differential equations. The governing nonlinear elastic wave equation with viscous damping is reduced through Lie symmetry analysis into four invariant ordinary differential equation forms, including scaling, translation, damped, and generalized damped symmetries. The proposed framework combines symmetry-aware solution reconstruction, composite residual and symmetry losses, and causality-based temporal weighting to improve the training stability and physical consistency of PINNs. Numerical experiments are performed using a fully connected neural network with four hidden layers, 128 neurons per layer, the tanh activation function, and the L-BFGS optimizer. The S-PINN solutions are compared with conventional PINNs and exact analytical references for all four symmetry-reduced cases. The results show that the proposed S-PINN framework provides faster convergence, lower loss, and improved solution accuracy. In Case IV, S-PINNs achieve a 35% faster convergence rate during the first 500 epochs and reduce the final loss from 3.8 for PINNs to 2.4. The S-PINN loss stabilizes after approximately 1000 epochs, whereas the PINN loss continues to oscillate with fluctuations up to 15%. The gradient norm remains within 0.5–1.5 for S-PINNs, compared with 0.2–2.5 for PINNs. At α = 0.4 , the S-PINN solution attains 98% agreement with the exact solution, and its maximum absolute error remains below 0.05, compared with 0.18 for the standard PINN. Contour comparisons further show less than 5% distortion for S-PINNs, while PINNs exhibit distortions up to 18%. These findings demonstrate that embedding Lie symmetries and causal temporal learning into PINNs constrains the solution space to physically admissible manifolds and improves the reliability of neural solvers for nonlinear wave propagation in computational mechanics.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Flood Susceptibility Mapping Using Calibrated Ensemble Machine Learning in the Indus River Basin, Pakistan
papers.abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping is an important component of spatial flood-risk assessment; however, conventional machine-learning approaches provide limited information about prediction reliability and spatial uncertainty. This study develops an uncertainty-aware flood susceptibility framework for the Indus River Basin (IRB), Pakistan, integrating satellite-derived flood observations, GIS-based environmental predictors, spatially blocked validation, probability calibration, ensemble learning, and uncertainty quantification. A flood inventory was derived from Landsat-9 observations of the July–August 2025 monsoon flood event, and environmental predictors were harmonized at a spatial resolution of 500 m. Four tree-based algorithms (LightGBM, XGBoost, Extra Trees, and HistGBM) were evaluated using five-fold spatially blocked cross-validation. Isotonic regression was applied to calibrate model probabilities, which were subsequently combined using a calibrated averaging ensemble (CAE). The CAE achieved mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and area under the precision–recall curve (PR-AUC) values of 0.878 and 0.837, respectively, and demonstrated improved probabilistic reliability compared with the individual classifiers. High- and very-high-susceptibility zones were concentrated across the central and lower Indus floodplains and major tributary corridors. Entropy analysis identified areas of model agreement and greater predictive uncertainty, while SHAP analysis highlighted drainage density, proximity to rivers and water bodies, the Standard Precipitation Index (SPI), and the topographic wetness index as influential predictors. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating spatial validation, probability calibration, ensemble learning, and uncertainty quantification for basin-scale flood susceptibility mapping. Because the analysis is based on a single flood event, the resulting maps represent event-informed susceptibility patterns rather than deterministic predictions of future flood extent or depth.

papers.title: Data-Driven and Nonlinear Control Methods for Autonomous Quadrotor Systems: Development and Evaluation of a Koopman-Based Predictive Control Framework
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction and control of quadrotor systems are challenging because their dynamics are nonlinear, coupled, and influenced by embedded flight-control behavior and environmental disturbances. This work investigates whether finite-dimensional bilinear Koopman models can provide sufficiently accurate short-horizon representations of nonlinear quadrotor dynamics for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC), and whether the resulting predictive framework can improve trajectory tracking under previously unseen disturbances. The methodology progresses from an analytical nonlinear pendulum to a reduced-order quadrotor with known governing equations, followed by data-driven identification and closed-loop control in PX4 Software-in-the-Loop with Gazebo, and finally prediction validation using physical DJI Tello EDU flight data. The pendulum and reduced-order studies establish the importance of bilinear state–input interactions introduced by nonlinear lifting. In a task-focused reduced-order comparison, the bilinear Koopman model reduced full-lap recursive three-dimensional position RMSE from 0.215 m to 0.005 m relative to an additive linear Koopman model, corresponding to a 97.66% reduction. In PX4–Gazebo, Koopman models were identified directly from simulated flight measurements and high-level velocity and yaw commands without explicitly supplying the complete rigid-body or embedded-controller equations. Under no-wind conditions, the learned model achieved a recursive approximately one-second three-dimensional position RMSE of 0.0081 m. A separate wind-conditioned proof-of-concept study showed that explicitly supplying wind information could substantially improve prediction under a tested disturbance. The final control architecture used a frozen no-wind-trained Koopman model as an outer predictive-correction layer while PX4 retained its cascaded stabilization loops. Wind speed and direction were not supplied to the predictor or optimizer during the final unseen-wind tests. Compared to the classical PX4 baseline under the same circular reference and wind conditions, the Koopman-NMPC architecture produced lower reported horizontal RMSE at every tested condition from 1 to 5 m/s East and under a diagonal 2 m/s East plus 2 m/s North disturbance. The largest observed reduction was 39.4% at 3 m/s East, while the benefit decreased to 7.4% at 5 m/s East. Finally, held-out DJI Tello flight data demonstrated physical short-horizon prediction accuracy, with position RMSE of approximately 5 mm over 0.22 s and below approximately 2 cm per axis over 0.55 s. The main contribution of this work is a practical progression from bilinear Koopman system identification to predictive quadrotor control, disturbance evaluation, baseline comparison, and physical-data validation within a unified framework. The results demonstrate that control-oriented bilinear Koopman representations can capture useful nonlinear command-response behavior directly from data while remaining suitable for short-horizon predictive optimization. This work lays the groundwork for future research in disturbance-conditioned and adaptive Koopman modeling, higher-dimensional vehicle representations, improved real-time optimization, and closed-loop physical-flight implementation. The framework therefore supports the continued development of data-driven nonlinear control methods for autonomous UAVs

papers.title: Actively seeking variability: effects of active learning and talker variability on novel word learning in adults
papers.abstract: Talker variability has been found to be both helpful and challenging for learners. For example, while adult word recognition is slowed down when the talker changes rapidly from trial to trial, this same talker variability can benefit learning non-native sound contrasts and production of novel words. However, all prior research has exposed participants to predetermined orders or variability conditions. Since research suggests that learners engage in active information seeking and it can benefit learning, here we ask whether adults seek out talker variability during word learning and how this variability influences performance. Active participants chose to hear words from 5 talkers on average, and hearing more talker variability for individual words predicted production and comprehension accuracy. While active learning was not beneficial, participants in the Passive condition performed better on the comprehension test. Results are consistent when cognates are excluded from the analyses. We discuss the results in the context of high variability phonetic training and active learning theories.

papers.title: Simulation of the Mzymta River Flow Using the Regularized Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: This study considers the simulation of hydrological processes in the Mzymta River (Russian Federation) using regularized Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). The Mzymta is the longest river in the Russian Federation and flows into the Black Sea. To formulate the boundary value problem, data on river topography (bottom profile) and hydrological measurements (time series of water level and discharge) from the gauging stations near the settlements of Rosa Khutor, Gorki-Gorod, Krasnaya Polyana, and Kazachiy Brod were collected. This study considers two modeling scales: the full-scale problem and a local-scale formulation for a short river segment, characterized by bed slope flattening, the development of a backwater–drawdown profile, and the occurrence of a hydraulic jump. The Saint-Venant system of equations was considered as a mathematical model. To solve this problem, we implemented PINNs. Two problem statements were considered: stationary and non-stationary. The full-scale simulation revealed that at the entire river scale, the flow rapidly establishes a normal depth profile, with all local perturbations being smoothed out by friction and thus indistinguishable at this resolution. In the unsteady case, the flow profile undergoes perturbations that propagate downstream in response to the time-varying sinusoidal inlet discharge. These perturbations propagate downstream at a finite speed, which is determined by the characteristic velocities of the shallow-water system. The local-scale formulation allowed us to capture the deviation of the flow profile from the normal depth and to study the backwater–drawdown problem, which involves the formation of a hydraulic jump both in stationary and non-stationary formulations. The formation of a hydraulic jump required the introduction of regularization into the loss function, since in the vicinity of the jump, the solution ceases to be smooth and experiences a discontinuity. To capture the discontinuity, we applied a method of relaxing the momentum equation term near the jump region. To enhance the sharpness of the jump, we additionally introduced a term that minimizes the width of the jump region. To properly account for all terms in the loss function, adaptive weighting of the coefficients was employed. Verification of the PINN against the fourth-order Runge–Kutta method is performed for the steady-state case, for both smooth solutions and solutions involving a hydraulic jump. The unsteady full-scale formulation is validated against the measured hydrograph between the Krasnaya Polyana and Kazachiy Brod gauging stations. A sensitivity analysis with respect to the river width and the Manning coefficient shows that these parameters strongly affect the depth profile. As a direction for future work, we outline an inverse formulation for the joint identification of the river width and Manning coefficient distributions along the river.

papers.title: Multifunctional Three-Dimensional-Printed Bio-Ink from Waterborne Polyurethane and Natural Antioxidants for Advanced Wound Dressings.
papers.abstract: The development of multifunctional wound dressings capable of simultaneously addressing oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and tissue regeneration remains a major challenge in advanced wound care. Here, we report a printable, bioactive 3D-printed dressing based on a synergistic bio-ink composed of waterborne polyurethane (WPU), pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant polyphenols (POM), and TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (TOCNF). POM was incorporated into the WPU matrix during in situ polymerization to introduce pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant and antibacterial functionality, while TOCNF served as a rheology modifier enabling extrusion-based direct ink writing. The resulting ink exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior, rapid viscosity recovery, and tunable yield stress, enabling successful, stable extrusion-based printing of multilayer architectures. Printed freeze-dried wound dressings exhibited highly interconnected porous structures (>90% porosity), robust swelling capacity, structural integrity under physiological conditions, and compressive stability after hydration. The incorporation of POM enhanced antibacterial performance against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli and provided strong free-radical scavenging activity. In vitro studies using HaCaT keratinocytes confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, enhanced metabolic activity, and significant attenuation of H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Notably, this wound dressing reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and improved cell survival under oxidative challenge. This work establishes a strategy for integrating natural antioxidant bioactives into printable polyurethane networks to produce structurally programmable, biologically active wound dressings. The combination of rheologically optimized printability, hierarchical porosity, and multifunctional bioactivity highlights the potential of this platform for advanced wound-dressing applications and other oxidative-stress-related tissue-repair strategies.

papers.title: Impact of total hip arthroplasty on multidimensional functioning and sleep in patients with hip osteoarthritis: A prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: BackgroundTotal hip arthroplasty (THA) is an established intervention for managing advanced osteoarthritis, offering substantial improvements in pain relief. However, relationship between sleep quality and functional outcomes after THA remains underexplored.ObjectiveThis longitudinal study aimed to evaluate changes in nocturnal sleep quality and daytime sleepiness and their association with functional recovery in 55 patients undergoing primary THA.MethodsPatients undergoing primary THA were enrolled in this prospective cohort study. Nocturnal sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, functional outcomes, and health-related quality of life were assessed preoperatively and at one, three, and sixxs months postoperatively using the PSQI, ESS, WOMAC, HOOS, and SF-36. Statistical analyses included Friedman's test with post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Kendall's tau correlations.ResultsWOMAC, PSQI, all HOOS dimensions, and both SF-36 components significantly improved over time. PSQI scores significantly decreased from the preoperative assessment to the postoperative follow-ups, indicating improved nocturnal sleep quality. In contrast, the median ESS score was 5 at each assessment, and no statistically significant group-level change in ESS was detected (p = 0.996). WOMAC and ESS were significantly correlated at one and six months, suggesting an association between functional recovery and daytime sleepiness at these timepoints.ConclusionsTHA was associated with significant improvements in pain, function, health-related quality of life, and nocturnal sleep quality up to six months postoperatively. No statistically significant group-level change in daytime sleepiness was detected. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, and larger prospective studies are needed to confirm them.

papers.title: Arthroplasty After Hemophilia Gene Therapy: Perioperative Implications and Clinical Experience
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gene therapy can provide sustained endogenous factor VIII (FVIII) or factor IX (FIX) expression, creating a perioperative phenotype that differs from both conventionally treated severe hemophilia and routine arthroplasty patients. Evidence for major joint replacement after gene therapy remains limited. AIM: To synthesize current clinical evidence on arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy and define practical implications for hemostatic management, venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary planning. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists were searched through September 2026 for direct arthroplasty reports, invasive-procedure studies after gene therapy, and current guidance relevant to surgery and thromboprophylaxis. RESULTS: Published evidence includes dedicated total knee and total hip arthroplasty reports, trial-level arthroplasty observations, and broader invasive-procedure datasets after valoctocogene roxaparvovec, etranacogene dezaparvovec, and fidanacogene elaparvovec. These data show that gene therapy may substantially reduce exogenous factor requirements, but they do not establish a validated FVIII or FIX threshold for arthroplasty. Current World Federation of Hemophilia guidance recommends achieving procedure-appropriate factor levels, with supplemental clotting factor concentrate when necessary. In patients whose factor activity has shifted toward mild-deficiency or nonhemophilic levels, standard arthroplasty VTE-prevention principles should not be withheld solely because of the historical diagnosis of hemophilia. CONCLUSION: Arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy should be managed as phenotype-based major surgery: procedure-appropriate hemostasis, immediate rescue-factor access, serial postoperative monitoring, and appropriately timed VTE prophylaxis remain essential.

papers.title: Strength Analysis of Polymers Comparing with Ti-6Al-4V Used as Orthopaedic Implants by Dynamic Analysis
papers.abstract: In human anatomy, the femur is the longest and largest bone. The selection of suitable materials for femoral bone implants is essential for ensuring structural stability, durability, and patient comfort. The present study investigates the mechanical behaviour of different femoral implant materials under dynamic loading conditions using Finite Element Analysis (FEA). The materials considered in this study include PEEK (Polyether Ether Ketone), PEEK 30C, polyurethane, Ti-6Al-4V, and S316L stainless steel. The mechanical response of these materials is evaluated by applying different loading conditions corresponding to patient body weights. The maximum displacement and von Mises stress are considered as the primary parameters for comparing implant performance. The density, Young’s modulus, and Poisson’s ratio of the selected materials are also taken into account to understand their influence on structural behaviour. Polymer-based materials such as PEEK, PEEK 30C, and polyurethane offer the potential advantage of reduced implant weight compared with conventional metallic materials, which may contribute to improved patient comfort. The FEA results provide insights into stress distribution and deformation in the implant, particularly in critical regions such as the femoral head and neck. The study aims to identify promising implant materials based on their mechanical response under dynamic loading. The findings can support preliminary material selection for femoral implants, while further experimental testing, fatigue evaluation, wear assessment, and biocompatibility studies are necessary to establish their suitability for long-term clinical applications. Thus it is concluded that polymer is a low density material it makes the patient to feel comfort to move his leg and the stresses obtained are within the allowable stress. Polymer materials has high corrosion resistance, wear resistance and also it is more bio-compatible to human body. So it is suggested that polymer material is suitable for the femur implantation.
