papers.title: Ship-bank interaction: a critical perspective review and future prospective
papers.abstract: The increasing volume of global maritime traffic requires the safe navigation of large vessels through restricted waterways, where ship-bank interactions can increase the risks of grounding, collision, and channel blockage. This review critically evaluates experimental, numerical, and simulation-based studies of ship-bank hydrodynamic interactions. The analysis shows that CFD generally provides more accurate predictions of surge and sway forces by capturing viscous and free-surface effects, particularly in shallow water, although considerable uncertainty remains in predicting yaw moments near banks under extremely shallow-water conditions. Potential-flow methods enable rapid parametric assessments but may underpredict lateral forces because of their inviscid formulation. Major research gaps include limited experimental uncertainty quantification, insufficient investigation of multi-degree-of-freedom drift motions, and conflicting surge-force trends associated with hull-specific flow dynamics. Future research should prioritize hybrid experimental-numerical frameworks, scale-effect quantification, and validated multi-DOF mathematical models incorporating external disturbances to enhance navigational safety.Highlights Review ship-bank interaction experimental and numerical studies.Comparative analysis of studies based on previous approaches.Displaying the differences across various conducted studies.Highlight the scientific issues that require more concern in future work.

papers.title: Two-stage cooperative optimisation of signal timing and vehicle trajectories for eco-driving at signalised intersections under HDV/CAV/CCAV mixed traffic
papers.abstract: The transportation sector accounts for approximately 20% of global energy consumption and is responsible for nearly 25% of global energy-related CO2 emissions, 75% of which come from road transport. Global energy consumption and CO2 emissions from transportation are projected to increase by more than 50% by 2030, and this energy consumption is causing environmental damage. As autonomous vehicles become more widespread, energy consumption issues in the new context of human-machine mixed driving are gradually attracting attention. To reduce energy consumption in emerging human-machine hybrid traffic flows and promote ecological driving, while accounting for the trend toward mixed traffic comprising autonomous and manually driven vehicles, this study proposes a method to guide manually driven vehicles at signalized intersections by having autonomous vehicles lead them. An ecological driving strategy based on a mixed-traffic-following model is established. The study designed a two-way, four-lane, cross-shaped, connected intersection scenario, employing a two-stage collaborative optimisation strategy for traffic signals and vehicle trajectories to coordinate the driving states of various vehicle types within the mixed fleet, thereby optimising following distances and speeds. By constructing vehicle energy consumption models and trajectory optimization models, effective reductions in vehicle energy consumption were achieved. Simulation results indicate that as the penetration rate of autonomous vehicles increases, the number of stops and energy consumption of vehicles in mixed traffic flow significantly decrease, validating the effectiveness of the proposed strategy and providing strong support for reducing carbon emissions.

papers.title: Early Perioperative Recovery Patterns Across Diverse Minimally Invasive Orthopedic Procedures: A Prospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Minimally invasive orthopedic surgery (MIOS) has been increasingly adopted to reduce surgical trauma and facilitate postoperative recovery. However, few datasets describe real-world early recovery across diverse minimally invasive procedures. This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 200 adult patients who underwent minimally invasive orthopedic surgery at a tertiary academic center between 15 December 2022 and 31 December 2024. Procedures included minimally invasive spine surgery, minimally invasive total knee arthroplasty (TKA), minimally invasive total hip arthroplasty (THA), percutaneous sacroiliac joint fusion (SI arthrodesis), and arthroscopic or percutaneous fixation procedures. Primary outcomes were hospital stay, time to independent ambulation, VAS pain score, and patient-reported functional outcome. Secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss in the operating room, complications, readmission, and reoperation. The median hospital stay was 2.1 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1.4-2.9), and the median time to independent ambulation was 1.6 days (IQR 1.1-2.1). Mean operative time was 91.1 ± 24.0 minutes, and mean estimated blood loss was 136.6 ± 47.7 mL. Preoperatively, patients had a mean VAS pain score of 7.2 ± 1.1, which decreased to 3.1 ± 0.8 at hospital discharge. There was a significant improvement in functional outcome for all procedure categories (p < 0.001). The overall incidence of complications was 7.5% (95% CI 3.8-11.2%). The 30-day readmission rate was 2.0% (n = 4), and the 90-day reoperation rate was 1.0% (n = 2). These findings characterize early perioperative recovery trajectories across five categories of minimally invasive orthopedic procedures, providing benchmark recovery timelines to support preoperative patient counseling and inform future comparative studies.

papers.title: Genetic algorithm-optimized state space neural operator for power plant data platforms
papers.abstract: Modern power plant data platforms need to manage large-scale operational data, which are heterogeneous and high-speed and are not stationary. High-computational models like Recurrent and Attention-based often have high computational cost, sensitivity to noise and load variations, and, in the attention-based case, catastrophic forgetting. To overcome these difficulties, this paper introduces a novel framework of GA-SSNOOP (Genetic Algorithm–Optimized State Space Neural Operator) to efficiently model a power plant system in the time domain. The framework combines continuous-time state-space neural operators and multi-objective Genetic Algorithm optimization to enhance the prediction accuracy, stability, and computational efficiency. Approximately 50,000 data points with 15–20 sensor variables were tested under a variety of operating conditions for both the Steam Turbine and the Boiler datasets. GA-SSNOOP unites the advantages of state space learning with the hyperparameter optimization of evolution, enabling it to capture the complex dynamics of the system and automatically determine the optimal model configuration. Results show a better forecasting performance than the baseline models of LSTM and Transformer, with the models converging faster, making lower prediction errors and consuming less memory. These results indicate the potential of GA-SSNOOP to scalable, real-time industrial analytics, intelligent monitoring and decision support in modern power plant environments.

papers.title: Dynamic Erosion Prediction of Tundish Refractories Based on Hybrid Deep Learning
papers.abstract: To quantify the CFD‐resolved thermal–mechanical erosion of tundish refractories in continuous steel casting, this study proposes a digital twin early warning model integrating multiphysical fields and hybrid deep learning. Combining CFD simulations and on‐site data, physical features were extracted and screened using PCC‐LASSO, with unreliable pressure boundaries actively removed. A PSO‐optimized BiLSTM–Transformer model was then constructed. By introducing target lag features and smoothed thermodynamic features state, the model synergistically captures both local temporal fluctuations and global cumulative erosion effects, overcoming the extrapolation limits of traditional regression models. Additionally, Monte Carlo Dropout is utilized to dynamically output a 95% prediction confidence interval for quantified risk assessment. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a significantly lower maximum absolute error (MaxAE) than benchmarks like SVR and XGBoost, exhibiting strong generalization across unseen operating conditions. Furthermore, SHAP attribution analysis shows a feature‐attribution pattern consistent with turbulence‐enhanced convective heat transfer driving the CFD‐resolved thermal–mechanical thinning within the enthalpy–porosity description. Ultimately, this research provides a highly reliable algorithmic pathway for predictive maintenance in complex metallurgical scenarios.

papers.title: Towards causal inference in materials informatics: methods, applications and opportunities
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has transformed materials screening, yet it optimises for statistical association rather than causation. This communication introduces causal inference frameworks, including structural causal models (SCMs), directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and the potential-outcomes framework, as a principled complement to ML in materials informatics. We clarify how these tools align with the process–structure–property–performance (PSPP) paradigm, make explicit the assumptions required for valid causal inference in materials datasets, contrast causal inference with explainable AI, and provide a concrete worked example of causal modelling in laser powder-bed fusion, together with pseudo-code for constraint-based causal discovery. We review emerging applications spanning nanocatalysis, additive manufacturing, welding, composites, coatings, and degradation modelling, outline methodological strategies integrating causal discovery with Bayesian uncertainty quantification and graph neural networks (GNNs), and close with a prioritised research roadmap for autonomous causal materials discovery.

papers.title: Metallosis Following Bipolar Hemiarthroplasty Due to Polyethylene Wear: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Metallosis following bipolar hemiarthroplasty is an uncommon complication that can result from wear of the concealed polyethylene bearing within the bipolar head.We report the case of a 54-year-old man who presented with six months of progressive right hip pain, four years after bipolar hemiarthroplasty for a transcervical fracture of the femoral neck.Laboratory investigations showed no evidence of infection.Radiographs and computed tomography demonstrated eccentric positioning of the femoral head within the bipolar cup, with peri-trochanteric and acetabular osteolysis and a contained supra-acetabular bone defect measuring approximately 2 × 2 cm.During revision surgery, extensive blackish discoloration of the periprosthetic tissues consistent with metallosis was observed.Examination of the retrieved bipolar head demonstrated complete wear-through of the inner polyethylene liner, resulting in direct metal-on-metal articulation between the inner and outer metal components and generation of substantial metallic debris.A two-stage revision was performed.Extended trochanteric osteotomy was required for femoral stem extraction, followed by extensive debridement and placement of an antibiotic cement spacer.After eight weeks, iliac crest bone grafting was performed for the acetabular defect and the patient underwent conversion to cementless total hip arthroplasty.Histopathological examination confirmed metallosis.At follow-up, the patient was pain-free and independently mobile.This case highlights that concealed polyethylene wear within a bipolar head can progress to direct metal-on-metal articulation, metallosis, osteolysis, and prosthetic failure.Eccentric positioning of the femoral head in a painful bipolar hemiarthroplasty should prompt careful evaluation for polyethylene bearing failure, even when inflammatory markers are normal.Early recognition and appropriate staged revision can facilitate management of extensive metallosis and bone loss.

papers.title: Hybrid dynamical system models for human–robot interaction
papers.abstract: With the increasing popularity of human-robot interaction (HRI), control systems are becoming more and more interesting and complicated because they need to coordinate continuous human movements and discrete robot decision-making in dynamic environments.The current strategies tend to be less flexible when working collaboratively, take longer to react and become less stable in interaction.This study presents a hybrid nonlinear statespace model, hybrid automata, Model Predictive Control (MPC), Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and Adaptive Hybrid Interaction Algorithm (AHIA) based Hybrid Dynamical Human-Robot Interaction (HD-HRI) framework for real-time human intent estimation and robot motion planning.The framework is assessed based on the accuracy of interaction, prediction of intent, trajectory tracking error, response latency, collision avoidance rate and task completion success.Experimental results confirm that 95.8% of the interactions are accurate, 94.9% of intents are correctly predicted, 21.6% of trajectory tracking errors is reduced, 18.4% of response latency is reduced, 97.3% of collisions are avoided, and 95.6% of the tasks are completed.The results prove that the proposed hybrid dynamical framework can be effectively implemented in practical applications, which can be reliable, stable, and efficient for human-robot collaboration.

papers.title: Driving on manifolds: A stochastic manifold mapping paradigm for generalizable end-to-end autonomous driving
papers.abstract: Developing generalist end-to-end autonomous driving systems requires balancing the retention of fundamental driving capabilities with the flexibility to adapt to diverse downstream objectives. Current paradigms struggle to reconcile these requirements. Direct regression methods rely on rigid representations that are prone to catastrophic forgetting during adaptation, while diffusion-based approaches are often limited by entangled policy representations and high computational costs. To bridge this gap, we present Driving On Manifolds (DOM), a novel framework based on the Stochastic Manifold Mapping (SMM) paradigm. DOM mathematically decomposes the driving problem into learning a reversible geometric mapping onto the action manifold and modeling a latent density over policy preferences. This topological separation confers two inherent advantages. First, the learned geometric mapping enables extensive synthetic data generation via latent sampling, allowing DOM to acquire intrinsic safety awareness by internalizing boundary constraints without relying on reactive external simulation. Second, it facilitates capability-preserving adaptation: the system aligns with downstream tasks (e.g., via Reinforcement Learning) by updating only the latent distribution and leveraging the exact likelihood for efficient fine-tuning, while the frozen geometric mapping structurally confines adaptation to the pre-trained manifold, substantially mitigating the degradation of established driving capabilities. Specifically, we instantiate this framework using a Manifold Normalizing Flow, driven by features from ContextFormer, a streamlined encoder designed for efficient environmental feature extraction. Validated on the NAVSIM benchmark, large-scale real-world datasets, and closed-loop real-world experiments, DOM achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates favorable scaling properties, offering a unified and scalable foundation for autonomous driving.

papers.title: Probabilistic Prediction of Rock Strength: Physics-Featured Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: Laboratory determination of uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) after in situ sampling is costly and slow. Coupling measurement while drilling (MWD) with machine learning can recover UCS in place. Most such models, however, return point estimates and quantify uncertainty only weakly. This study compiled 161 records from seven sources. Records that recur across sources were removed, leaving 111 unique records, 93 of them soft rock with torque below 100 kN·m. PG-GPR was fitted to these 93 records and checked by five-fold cross-validation with ten random seeds. Against a baseline that used the same kernel on the four raw drilling channels, R2 rose from 0.925 ± 0.011 to 0.964 ± 0.006 and mean absolute error fell from 3.19 ± 0.22 MPa to 2.25 ± 0.15 MPa. At comparable empirical coverage, mean interval width fell from 14.45 ± 0.43 MPa to 8.60 ± 0.25 MPa, and CRPS fell from 2.37 ± 0.12 to 1.65 ± 0.12. Leave-one-source-out scoring of all 93 held-out records together gives R2 = 0.463 and RMSE = 12.11 MPa.

papers.title: Multi-output Gaussian process regression for uncertainty-aware sound insulation prediction in mass timber floors
papers.abstract: Reliable analysis of sound insulation of mass timber floors requires extensive and time-consuming measurements. Such multi-layer assemblies exhibit a complex insulation behavior under both airborne and structure-borne excitation, governed by the interactions between individual layers. In addition, there are uncertainties associated with timber as a building material, its processing, and measurement of the built assemblies. In order to reduce the measurement effort in the long term, a prediction approach that both accounts for these uncertainties in the model and quantifies them in its predictions is required. This study introduces multi-output Gaussian process regression models for the prediction of airborne and impact sound insulation spectra from 50 Hz to 5 kHz. Single-number quantities are derived from the prediction distributions using a Monte Carlo method. The models are developed on a curated dataset of laboratory measurements of mass timber floor assemblies. To also account for nominal inputs, the models are augmented by embeddings that are trained end-to-end with the remaining model parameters under a common objective, the negative log marginal likelihood. The predictions distinguish aleatoric, i.e. measurement-related uncertainty, from epistemic uncertainty that additional knowledge could reduce. Averaged over the frequency bands, the predictions reach mean absolute errors of 2.1 dB for airborne and 3.9 dB for impact sound insulation, while the derived single-number quantities are predicted to within 1.4 dB and 2.2 dB, respectively.

papers.title: Shifting Ground: Architectural Maneuver and Economic Deterrence in the Era of Autonomous Cyber Adversaries
papers.abstract: The proliferation of autonomous, agentic AI in offensive cyber operations has fundamentally altered the offense-defense balance. As evidenced by recent reporting on automated intrusions achieving marginal costs of approximately $50 per successful breach, the traditional defensive cycle(detection, alerting, and human-gated response) is outpaced by machine-speed execution. This paper proposes a structural framework, termed "Shifting Ground," for defending networks against autonomous adversaries. Drawing on systems thinking, organizational theory, and recent literature on moving target defense, we argue that static fortifications are inherently obsolete against learning agents. Instead, defense must prioritize the invalidation of the adversary's world model at the moment of commitment, paired with economic attrition models. The paper further delineates the boundaries of this framework, utilizing a typology of adversarial threat models (bounded versus unbounded budgets, in-battlespace versus out-of-battlespace vectors) to prevent the scope overreach common in commercial security postures. Finally, it addresses the necessary institutional architecture, arguing that technical postures are insufficient without independent verification, sustainable defense economics, and organizational cultures that institutionalize dissent.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Remote Sensing for Freshwater Quality Monitoring: A Systematic Review of Methods, Applications, Model Performance, and Research Gaps
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) integrated with remote sensing offers a scalable approach to freshwater‐quality monitoring, potentially extending the spatial and temporal coverage of conventional field measurements. However, evidence on model performance, validation, and transferability remains heterogeneous. This systematic review synthesized evidence on AI and remote sensing for freshwater‐quality monitoring, focusing on remote‐sensing platforms, target parameters, AI/machine‐learning (ML) methods, predictive performance, validation, and generalizability. Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore were searched for studies published from March 2000 to April 30, 2026. Study selection followed PRISMA 2020 guidance. Eligible studies used remote‐sensing data with AI/ML or deep‐learning methods to assess freshwater quality. Data on sensors, target variables, algorithms, performance metrics, validation, uncertainty, explainability, and reproducibility were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Thirty‐one primary studies (S01–S31) were included and consistently cross‐referenced throughout the manuscript and supplementary tables. Sentinel‐2/MSI (16/31; 51.6%) and Landsat (10/31; 32.3%) were the most frequently used platforms. Chlorophyll‐a (15/31; 48.4%), turbidity (11/31; 35.5%), and total suspended solids (8/31; 25.8%) were the most studied parameters. Random Forest (17/31; 54.8%), support‐vector methods (11/31; 35.5%), and artificial neural networks (10/31; 32.3%) were commonly applied. Internal validation predominated, while independent temporal, spatial, cross‐site, cross‐region, cross‐sensor, and external validation was uncommon. Uncertainty, explainability, and data/code availability were inconsistently reported. Overall, evidence supports strong within‐study predictive performance more than environmental generalizability. Future research should prioritize independent multi‐site and multi‐season validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable AI, standardized reporting, and reproducible workflows.

papers.title: Influence of geometric and manufacturing parameters on the compressive behaviour of FFF lattices
papers.abstract: Abstract Lattice structures manufactured by fused filament fabrication (FFF) enable the mechanical response of architected materials to be tailored through geometric and manufacturing parameters. However, the relative importance of these factors across different lattice architectures remains insufficiently quantified within a consistent experimental framework. This study investigates the influence of geometric and manufacturing parameters on the compressive response of three lattice architectures (octet‐truss, re‐entrant and gyroid) manufactured from glycol‐modified poly(ethylene terephthalate). A full factorial design of experiments was employed as an exploratory screening approach to investigate the effects of the number of unit cells, wall thickness and layer height. Specific yield strength and specific energy absorption were evaluated, while analysis of variance and Lenth's method were used to identify and compare parameter‐related trends across the investigated architectures. Within the investigated parameter ranges, the octet and re‐entrant lattices exhibited clearer trends associated with geometric parameters, particularly wall thickness and number of unit cells, whereas no comparable effect was observed for layer height. The gyroid architecture showed a more homogeneous response, with the effects of the investigated parameters being less clearly resolved within the adopted experimental design. The results provide preliminary evidence that the relative influence of geometric and manufacturing parameters differs between lattice architectures. By comparing distinct topologies under consistent manufacturing and testing conditions, this exploratory study identifies parameter‐related trends that can support the design of future replicated experiments and more robust investigations of FFF lattice structures. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: Effect of Outrunning the Aquifer in Heterogeneous Water Drive Gas Reservoirs
papers.abstract: Water-drive gas reservoirs (WDGRs) are often affected by early water breakthrough and reduced recovery, particularly in heterogeneous and stratified systems. Producing gas at elevated rates outrunning the aquifer has been proposed to delay water encroachment and enhance recovery factor (RF). This study conducted nearly 1,000 reservoir simulation runs to evaluate the effects of aquifer size, heterogeneity (Lorenz Coefficient), stratification, reservoir dip, vertical permeability, and gas type (dry and wet) on outrunning performance. Gas condensate systems were excluded due to condensate dropout and liquid accumulation below the dew point, which can distort production behavior. Results indicate that outrunning can increase RF by up to 15% in moderately heterogeneous systems (LC ≈ 0.3), while highly heterogeneous cases (LC ≈ 0.9) exhibit more variable responses, including modest RF reductions. Stratification introduces additional complexity, with RF reductions of up to 6.45% at low aquifer sizes; however, this negative effect diminishes as aquifer strength increases, reflecting a strong interaction between layering and aquifer support. Intermediate aquifer volumes consistently provide the highest RF improvement, whereas very large aquifers reduce effectiveness due to water compressibility effects. Reservoir dip also influences performance, with low-dip systems showing the highest gains, while gas type has minimal impact. Vertical permeability sensitivity shows no consistent trend, indicating the need for dual-porosity–dual-permeability representations. Formal probabilistic uncertainty quantification (e.g., Monte Carlo analysis) was not included in this study. Overall, outrunning is conditionally effective and strongly governed by coupled reservoir and aquifer characteristics.

papers.title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
papers.abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,β)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.

papers.title: Efficient Deep Gaussian Process Surrogates via Mini-Batch Latent MAP Estimation
papers.abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are flexible surrogate models for computer experiments with nonstationary response surfaces, but inference over their latent representations remains computationally challenging. Existing methods typically rely on variational inference or Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), which impose variational-family assumptions or require costly posterior sampling. We propose the latent maximum-a-posteriori deep Gaussian process (LaMP-DGP), which uses gradient-based optimization to obtain MAP estimates of the latent representations and enables efficient probabilistic prediction through linked-GP calculations. To scale LaMP-DGP to large datasets, we develop a mini-batch optimization algorithm and, under a polynomial mini-batch bias-decay condition, establish a stationarity bound for latent-state optimization that motivates a growing batch-size schedule. Across numerical experiments and real-data analyses, LaMP-DGP provides consistently competitive predictive performance relative to doubly stochastic variational inference, stochastic gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and fully Bayesian Vecchia DGP inference. Computationally, LaMP-DGP is substantially faster than the Vecchia MCMC approach while remaining broadly competitive with the stochastic-gradient alternatives. These results position LaMP-DGP as a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for DGP inference. An R package, "LaMPDGP", is available for implementing the proposed method.

papers.title: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion
papers.abstract: This paper presents a two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control. In the first stage, we train a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics combined with full humanoid kinematics. In the second stage, the frozen ROM policy is rolled out online to generate references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order dynamics model. Learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space enables us to generate references over a broad command space and over multiple locomotion strategies using a single unified framework. We demonstrate the approach on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, achieving longitudinal velocities from -2.0 m/s to 2.8 m/s, lateral velocities up to +-1.0 m/s, angular velocities up to +-3.0 rad/s, one-legged hopping, and continuous transitions across the commands, all using one unified reference policy and one whole-body tracking policy.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Latent Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series
papers.abstract: Time-series data play an important role in various tasks, such as weather forecasting, web traffic analysis, and speech recognition. Recently, pioneering studies have increasingly adopted Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) based encoders to learn time-series representations through latent-space prediction. However, they often overlook the underlying factors governing transitions between time-series observations. In this work, we hypothesize that explicitly modeling the information behind changes in time series can facilitate time-series modeling. Building on this hypothesis, we propose ACTS-WM, a self-supervised latent action-conditioned world model framework for time-series analysis. First, we introduce a latent action modeling approach that infers the underlying information behind time-series transitions as latent actions, without requiring explicit action annotations. We then develop a JEPA-based encoder and an action-conditioned world model to predict target time-series representations conditioned on the learned latent actions and task information. We evaluate ACTS-WM across 4 representative tasks on 22 datasets from diverse domains, covering univariate and multivariate forecasting and classification. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ACTS-WM can improve downstream performance over pretrained JEPA-based encoders by learning complementary representations.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class.   We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length. On a bounded response domain, we bound excess length linearly in $L^1$ density error at fixed calibration size, without requiring a uniform positive lower bound on the true density. We also bound selection-pool and resampling errors. Under explicit growth conditions, the selected procedure approaches the same oracle while the calibration size remains fixed.   Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, prediction-set length, and runtime with existing methods.   In targeted low-coverage and strong-shift comparisons, inverse-density selection yields shorter mean sets in most cases and lower mean runtime than the evaluated weighted baselines, with some differences in achieved coverage.

papers.title: Echo: Scaling Visual Reinforcement Learning with Off-policy Experience
papers.abstract: Scaling visual reinforcement learning (RL) with GPU-accelerated simulation is computationally expensive due to rendering and visual-policy inference costs. Consequently, two-stage teacher--student distillation is commonly used to train visual policies, but introduces an imitation gap. In this preliminary study, we introduce \echomethod{}, \textbf{a single-stage off-policy RL framework that scales experience collection without proportionally increasing visual computation}. Through \textbf{inverse distillation}, a state-based auxiliary policy imitates the evolving visual policy and collects inexpensive, unrendered experience. Echo leverages this experience for off-policy value learning, directly improving the visual policy through a shared privileged critic. We instantiate \echomethod{} with FastTD3 and evaluate it on three visual control tasks and two dexterous manipulation tasks in Genesis. Relative to \sdpgmethod{} under the evaluated configurations, Echo reduces time to reference returns by an average of \textbf{60\% across the three locomotion tasks} and \textbf{56\% across both hand tasks}, while improving peak mean returns by \textbf{62\% and 12\%}, respectively. Both hand tasks also achieve higher mean returns at matched simulator-transition budgets. These initial results suggest that scaling off-policy experience is a promising approach to efficient direct visual RL.

papers.title: DropFENO: A Data-Free, Physics-Based Operator-Learning Framework for Droplet Equilibria on Mixed-Wettability Patterned Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study whether the equilibrium of a drop on a chemically patterned wall, and the capillary forces that the pattern exerts on it, can be learned from the free energy alone, without solution data. We introduce DropFENO (Droplet Free-Energy Neural Operator), in which Fourier (FNO), tensor-factorised Fourier (TFNO) and wavelet (WNO) neural operators are trained in two and three dimensions on the diffuse-interface free energy of the drop, with its volume and centroid constraints imposed as penalties. The predictions are tested with the virtual-work (Hellmann--Feynman) theorem: the force exerted by the pattern on a held drop is a wall integral of the equilibrium field which, for a drop straddling a wettability step, reduces identically to the contact-line law $F=σΔ\cosθ\,L$. DropFENO reproduces this law and the energy landscape of a drop crossing a step, and reproduces the pinning of the receding contact line less accurately. The residual error lies in the soft modes of the capillary energy (small displacements of the interface and the contact line). This explains why the energy is predicted accurately while contact-line positions are not, and why on striped walls the operators return Cassie-like states instead of the edge-pinned states whose anisotropic apparent angles the reference minimiser shares with lattice Boltzmann simulations. On held-out patterned walls the median energy of the predictions lies $\NdEmedRandFnoTwo$ of the free-drop energy above the best known minimum (FNO, two dimensions), at about one hundredth of the cost of a per-instance minimisation, and a refinement by a classical solver started from the prediction returns the reference state in almost all cases.

papers.title: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction
papers.abstract: Robots, autonomous vehicles, and consumer 360° cameras use fisheye lenses for wide fields of view (FoVs). Simulation-ready digital twins require photorealistic rendering across the full FoV and an aligned collision mesh. However, prior fisheye Gaussian Splatting methods only rasterize up to 180° and do not produce meshes, while Gaussian surface reconstruction methods assume pinhole training images. We present GOFish, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction method to train directly on fisheye images, rasterize FoVs beyond 180°, and extract an aligned mesh from the same scene. Calibrated densification recovers the surface across the entire FoV, while Calibrated Mip Filtering and Wide-Angle Appearance Modeling keep pixel blur and lens falloff out of the scene and mesh. Across the 200° FIORD and 205° FullCircle benchmarks, GOFish improves PSNR over the best prior method by 2.28 and 1.97 dB, respectively. It also outperforms fisheye rendering baselines within their own FoVs and achieves the highest mesh F-score on FIORD and the main ScanNet++ set. Together, the Gaussian scene and mesh form a LiDAR-free, simulation-ready digital twin that renders in real time, ray traces the full FoV, and provides collision geometry.

papers.title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation
papers.abstract: Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) replace the hyperparameter refitting of Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass, at the cost of a prior that is fixed at meta-training time. We show empirically that a PFN's predictive log-likelihood falls increasingly behind that of a refitted GP as the objective function's lengthscale grows beyond the mode of the PFN's meta-training prior, and that this deficit carries over to optimisation performance. To correct the mismatch without retraining the network, we introduce Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping. Per-dimension lengthscales are estimated by kernel target alignment, and an affine rescaling of the input space maps the objective onto the lengthscale the PFN expects, with a trust region around the anchor determining which observations are retained, leaving the PFN's $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot N^2)$ inference cost unchanged. On functions drawn from a Matérn-3/2 kernel, ATR warping improves optimisation performance of the PFN at both extremes of the lengthscale range. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/Trust-Region-Warping-For-PFNs.

papers.title: Population-balance-based semi-empirical and machine learning modeling of electrostatic crude oil dewatering: Asymptotic reduction, identifiability, and robustness across scales
papers.abstract: Electrostatic crude oil dewatering is governed by coupled droplet aggregation and fragmentation mechanisms arising from electrohydrodynamic interactions. In this work, a physics-informed semi-empirical model is derived through an asymptotic reduction of the population balance equation (PBE), yielding a closed-form relation for the residual basic sediment and water content at the coalescer oil outlet ( BS & W o ) as a function of the ratio of breakup-to-coalescence rate coefficients. The formulation preserves mechanistic consistency while enabling parameter identifiability and rigorous uncertainty quantification. The semi-empirical model is benchmarked against multiple machine learning approaches using two datasets characterized by distinct levels of operational excitation: a pilot-scale dataset with broad variability and an industrial offshore dataset with restricted operating conditions and temporal fluctuations. A unified validation framework combining global sensitivity analysis, parametric correlation assessment, shuffled cross-validation, and chronological validation is employed to distinguish interpolation accuracy from forward temporal robustness. Results show that the asymptotic PBE reduction captures the dominant nonlinear structure across scales and remains stable under temporal distribution shifts. In contrast, flexible machine learning models achieve high interpolation performance but exhibit sensitivity to restricted excitation domains. The study highlights the structural role of dataset excitation in practical identifiability and generalization in multiphase separation systems

papers.title: ANALISIS PENERAPAN METODE RESUME DALAM PROSES PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN GURU MADRASAH IBTIDAIYAH
papers.abstract: Learning in higher education requires students to actively obtain, process, and convey information. The resume method, which involves summarizing learning material by selecting main ideas and rewriting them systematically in one's own words, is one strategy that can encourage such involvement. However, its implementation does not always achieve the intended learning objectives. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the resume method in the learning process of fourth-semester students of the Islamic Elementary School Teacher Education (PGMI) Study Program at STAIN Majene in the 2025–2026 academic year. This research used a qualitative approach with a descriptive design. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were collected from 42 students who had experienced learning with the resume method using a questionnaire distributed via Google Form. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The results show that most students had positive perceptions of the resume method. The method helps students understand learning material more deeply, develops analytical and critical thinking skills, and fosters learning independence. Nevertheless, students faced obstacles, including difficulty identifying main information, limited time, and the large amount of material to be summarized. The effectiveness of the method is strongly influenced by the lecturer's clear instructions, examples, and feedback. In conclusion, the resume method can serve as an alternative active learning strategy in PGMI, provided it is well designed and supported by lecturer guidance.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration in Machine Learning Models Using Bayesian Frameworks
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is a critical requirement for trustworthy machine learning, particularly in safety-critical applications such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. Modern neural networks frequently produce overconfident predictions due to poor probabilistic calibration, limiting their reliability under distributional shift and data scarcity. While Bayesian methods provide a principled framework for modeling both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, a unified comparative evaluation under consistent experimental conditions has been lacking. This study systematically compares four model classes under controlled regression and classification tasks: deterministic neural networks, Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, and Gaussian processes. Evaluation is conducted using strictly proper scoring rules; negative log-likelihood and the Brier score, alongside the expected calibration error and predictive entropy. Results demonstrate systematic differences in uncertainty reliability across model classes: Gaussian processes achieve superior calibration in low-data regimes, while Monte Carlo dropout provides a scalable approximation with competitive performance. Deterministic networks consistently exhibit overconfidence as measured by expected calibration error. These findings motivate further development of scalable, theoretically grounded UQ methods for modern machine learning systems.

summary_en.motivation: Trustworthy deployment of machine learning in safety-critical settings requires reliable uncertainty estimates, yet a consistent comparative evaluation of common UQ approaches has been missing.
summary_en.method: Four model classes—deterministic networks, Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, and Gaussian processes—are compared under controlled regression and classification tasks using strictly proper scoring rules and calibration metrics.
summary_en.result: Gaussian processes yield the best calibration in low-data regimes, Monte Carlo dropout offers a scalable approximation with competitive performance, and deterministic networks are consistently overconfident.
summary_en.validation: Models are evaluated on standard regression and classification benchmarks using negative log-likelihood, Brier score, expected calibration error, and predictive entropy.
